persons.name: Defiant Gatekeeper
persons.digest:
Defiant Gatekeeper describes the week as a global correction: the S&P 500 fell about 2% and the Nasdaq 4.5%, its biggest correction since late June. On Wednesday annual CPI came in at 3.7% against 3.6% expected, with core CPI at 2.6%; Thursday's monthly PPI was 1.3% versus 0.6% expected and Friday's core PPI was 0.7%.

The real oddity is in bonds: the 10-year yield first jumped above 5.3% and then fell to about 5.05%. In his view bond investors expect a sharp economic deterioration tied to AI; a **CoreWeave** bond fell below 80 cents and its CDS spread rose to about 1,000 bps, **Oracle**'s CDS hit a record 288 bps and **SK Hynix** is down about 57% from its summer peak. The 2026 US budget deficit was reported at $1.992 trillion (about 6% of GDP) and the semiconductor index fell about 12% on the week. Using a weather analogy he tells viewers to be careful in a storm, watch the 2s10s spread at about 0.3 and track OpenAI's and Anthropic's performance.

items.title: AI meltdown...and dancing bond bros
items.summary: The video covers the weekly correction: the S&P 500 fell about 2% and the Nasdaq 4.5%. CPI on Wednesday (3.7% vs 3.6% expected) and core CPI (2.6%) beat expectations, Thursday's monthly PPI was 1.3% (expected 0.6%) and Friday's core PPI was 0.7% (expected 0.3%). The 10-year yield dropped from above 5.3% to 5.05%; he argues this is because the bond market assumes the economy equals AI and that AI weakness would collapse the economy. A CoreWeave bond fell below 80% of par, its CDS spread rose to about 1,000 bps (implying a 63% default probability); Oracle's CDS hit a record 288 bps and SK Hynix is about 57% below its summer peak. The US budget deficit is $1.992 trillion (~6% of GDP) and the semiconductor index fell ~12% on the week. He concludes that the 2s10s spread (about 0.3) should be watched, that OpenAI's and Anthropic's performance will decide confidence, and that caution is warranted in stormy weather.
